thesis: The episode argues that Uber is a category-defining investment currently in a strong position, driven by rapid growth in suburban ridesharing and new transportation initiatives expected to account for half of future growth. The speaker highlights a shift in shareholding toward fundamental long-only investors and notes that the resolution of the control issue allowed the company to focus on building, describing it as a 'hit of the century' for its early investor.

claims.claim: The speaker states that Uber's category position versus DoorDash is strong and constructive.
claims.quote: As we built out selection in urban centers, our category position versus DoorDash is actually quite constructive, really strong, we are looking to break into the suburbs.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that expanding ridesharing into the suburbs is a fast-growing part of the business.
claims.quote: Now we are expanding ridesharing into the suburbs now, and it's a pretty fast-growing part of our business.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that new transportation initiatives will account for 50% of Uber's growth.
claims.quote: If we do it right, 50% of our growth will come from these new initiatives that really didn't exist.

claims.claim: The speaker believes the stock price is generally working and the company is in a good place.
claims.quote: We're now seeing a stock price that generally is working. I'll tell you, when we're in the middle of it, it was tough. After the IPO, after the lockup, Travis sold all those shares.

claims.claim: The speaker believes the shareholding is moving to fundamental long-only players who will be shareholders for the next 10 years.
claims.quote: I think we're now in a good place, which is the shareholding is moving from either some of the startup folks or hedge funds to fundamental long-only players, who hopefully they'll be shareholders for the next 10 years.

claims.claim: The speaker describes Uber as a category-defining company and investment.
claims.quote: This was one of the hits of the century. This is a category-defining company and investment.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Walmart uses Uber's fulfillment services but is not in the marketplace.
claims.quote: For example, Walmart isn't in a marketplace because they're Walmart, they have an incredible brand, et cetera, but they use our fulfillment services.

claims.claim: The speaker states that the vision is for local grocers to out-Amazon.
claims.quote: More and more, our vision is we essentially want the local grocer to out-Amazon Amazon.

claims.quote: That one, he got Softbank in, but it stopped the power struggle because then no one could control the company. That was actually a real secondary benefit.
